_comment: Every claim-bearing line on the site lives here with its source. Page files import these by id; they never contain a statistic or a citation inline. If a line has no source, it is not a claim and does not belong in this file. `verify_before_launch: true` means the wording or the link must be checked by a human against the source before publishing.

who_prevalence.text: The World Health Organization estimates it affects roughly 10 percent of women and girls of reproductive age worldwide, which is around 190 million people.

diagnostic_delay.text: Studies have found the delay between first symptoms and a diagnosis is commonly between four and eleven years, and a large part of that delay is people not being believed.
diagnostic_delay.required_phrasing: commonly reported OR studies have found; never a bare number
diagnostic_delay.verify_note: The four to eleven year range comes from the brief. The ACOG release discusses diagnostic delay; the scoping review reports 6 to 11.7 years. Confirm the range wording against the linked sources, or narrow the range, before launch.

acog_clinical_diagnosis.text: In March 2026, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists published a clinical practice guideline saying that a clinical diagnosis, made from your symptoms, your history and a physical examination, is enough for a clinician to begin treatment. Laparoscopy is not required first.
acog_clinical_diagnosis.source_label: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 11, March 2026
acog_clinical_diagnosis.usage: educational context only, never a product claim

eshre_diary.text: The European Society of Human Reproduction and Embryology's 2022 guideline says patients are encouraged to keep a diary of their symptoms to support the history-taking process.
eshre_diary.usage: educational context only, never a product claim
eshre_diary.verify_note: Confirm the ESHRE URL still resolves and that the quoted sentence matches the guideline text.

translation_pairs.her_words: It hurts when I go to the bathroom, especially during my period.
translation_pairs.icd10_note: No ICD-10 code. No verified symptom code exists, so Emenla prints none.

product_facts._comment: Statements about what the app does. Source is the app itself; each must remain true of the shipped build.

on_device.text: Data lives in the app's own private on-device database. There is no server and no user database.

speech.text: Speech recognition runs on the device. No audio leaves the phone and no recording is kept.

photos.text: Photos are copied into the app's private storage. They are never uploaded and never written back to your photo library.

no_tracking.text: No analytics of any kind. No ads, no ad identifiers, no third-party trackers, no crash reporting, no remote configuration, no tracking prompt.

no_account.text: No account, nothing to sign into. Emenla does not collect an email address.

notifications.text: Notifications are local only. No push service, no device token.

purchase_exception.text: Logging is free forever. The optional summary export is an Apple in-app purchase handled through RevenueCat, which receives an anonymous purchase identity and your purchase status. It never receives your symptoms, notes, photos, cycle dates or your name.

gdpr.text: Under GDPR, health data is special category data under Article 9. That is exactly why Emenla has no server.

cyclical.text: The word "cyclical" is never taken from a sentence. Emenla only uses it after counting your logged days against your logged period starts. Concepts come from your words. Qualifiers come from your data.

competitor_true_claim.text: Other apps turn a symptom log into a document for a clinician. What Emenla does differently is print your own sentence beside every clinical term, with its source, and refuse to say "cyclical" until it has counted.
competitor_true_claim.source: brief; Endolog ships log-to-PDF, so the wider claim is not sayable
